transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Monkey! You useless, flea-bitten ape! The horse is gone, the scripture-bags are gone, and the Master is weeping! You said you'd secure it before you left! Tripitaka is going to blame me, I just know it!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Calm yourself, Pigsy! I'll soon set things right. There's no need to bellow and carry on so. I'll find the horse and the bags in no time flat. Just stay here and keep watch; I'll be back with everything before you can count to ten.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Calm myself"? How can I calm myself, you mangy monkey?! It was *your* job! You're always swaggering about how mighty you are, how you can see a thousand *li*, but you couldn't even see a thief under your own nose! And now the Master is crying, blaming *me* because I was left here to "keep watch"! What good is watching when the horse is already gone?! What am I supposed to watch, the empty space where the scriptures used to be? This is all your fault!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Enough! Cease your blubbering! I, Sun Wukong, am not one to shirk responsibility. If I erred, I'll make amends. But it's no use standing here like a pair of petulant children. We must act, and act swiftly. I'll go in search of the horse and the bags. You, Pigsy, should ready yourself to defend the camp should any miscreant come upon us in my absence. We'll have everything sorted before the day is done.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Cease my blubbering"? I'm not blubbering, I'm stating facts! Facts that point directly to *you*, Great Sage Equal to Heaven, being utterly useless when it actually matters! And now you want me to "defend the camp"? Defend it with what, my good looks? The horse is gone, the bags are gone, we're sitting ducks out here! What if it's some demon with a taste for plump, handsome monks? What am I supposed to do, challenge him to a poetry contest? No, no, you need to find them *now*. And don't you dare come back without everything, or the Master will have both our hides! He'll be putting that "tightening spell" on *me* next, I just know it!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Peace! Pigsy, you're right to be concerned, but let's not indulge in more than our share of panic. The camp is not defenseless, you have your enchanted mace, and I've taught you a thing or two about fending off fiends. I'll be back with the horse and the bags before the sun sets, and you'll see to it that no harm befalls our camp in my absence. Now, quit your whining and take up your post. I'll be off to track the trail of that errant nag. Remember, Pigsy, it's not the size of the opponent that matters, but the size of your... *ahem*... heart. Now, be alert!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Not the size of the opponent, but the size of my... *ahem*... heart"? Ha! Easy for you to say, Monkey, with your impenetrable hide and your golden cudgel that can shrink to a needle! My mace is heavy, and my heart is currently pounding like a drum in a thunderstorm! And what if it's a fiend that just *eats* maces? Or a fiend that turns invisible? I can't track invisible fiends! You're just trying to get rid of me so you don't have to hear me complain anymore!

This is a disaster, I tell you! A complete disaster! If those scriptures are damaged, the Master will never forgive us. And it's all because you couldn't keep an eye on things! Just make sure you actually *find* them this time, you hear me? Don't come back with some half-baked story about a "minor setback" or a "small misunderstanding"! Bring back the horse, bring back the bags, and bring them back *now*! Or I'm telling the Master everything, and I mean *everything*!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy! Enough of this! I'm off to find the horse and the bags, and I'll be back with them before you can say 'roc's nest'! You'll do well to remember that we're in this together, and that no amount of squabbling will bring them back faster. Now, take your post, and don't you dare come after me. If I have to deal with your kvetching in addition to tracking a horse, it'll be a true test of my monkey patience. Be on guard, and I'll be back with the horse and the bags posthaste!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Roc's nest"? What does a roc's nest have to do with anything, you half-witted ape?! You just make up phrases when you don't know what to say! And I'm not "kvetching"! I'm expressing legitimate concerns about our eternal salvation, which is currently trotting off into the wilderness on the back of a stolen horse!

Fine! Go! But don't expect me to be whistling a happy tune while you're gone! I'll stand guard, yes, I'll stand guard... but if anything else goes missing, or if some monstrous fiend comes sniffing around for a tasty pig-snout, don't you dare blame *me*! You brought this upon us with your carelessness! Just hurry up, you hear me? Hurry up! Before the Master's tears turn into a flood and drown us all!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, Pigsy, Pigsy... You're like a烦 (fán,烦) in my ear! But enough of this. I'll be back with the horse and the bags, and if we're to be drowned by the Master's tears, let it be. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

Just remember whose fault it is when you're explaining yourself to the Bodhisattva! And don't you dare think I won't recount your failings, because I most certainly will! Every single one!

Just go already! And don't you dare come back empty-handed! If you think the Master's tears are bad, wait till you see his temper when he finds out we've lost everything *again* because of your fancy naps and careless guarding! Hurry, Monkey! Hurry!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, I'm gone. Remember your duty, and I'll be back with the horse and the bags. If not, you can tell the Master... and Guanyin... and all the heavens that Sun Wukong has failed. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

Just go! Go! And don't you dare come back without everything! I'll be here, *watching* the empty space where the horse and bags were, all thanks to you! Don't let me down, Monkey, or I swear... I'll tell the Master every single detail! Every last one! And he'll be furious! Just hurry, you hear me?! Hurry!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, enough! Your words are like a swarm of mosquitoes, but I must away. The horse and the bags will be returned, or I'm no son of the Dragon King. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, you've made your point. Now, I'm off to retrieve our goods. Remember, we're a team, and I'll not let you down. Or Tripitaka. Or Guanyin. Or... anyone.
